units.rightText: Now brace yourself like a man; Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?

units.leftText: Who determined its measures, if you know? What were its foundations fastened on?

units.rightText: Who set the wild donkey free? I made the wilderness his home

units.rightText: He scorns the tumult of the city He roams the mountains for pasture,

units.rightText: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness?

units.leftText: Moreover the LORD answered Job, “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty?
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Job: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty?

units.rightText: Then Job answered the LORD: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You?

units.leftText: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind:
units.rightText: I have spoken once, but I have no answer — Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:

units.leftText: “Now brace yourself like a man. Will you even annul my judgment?
units.rightText: “Now brace yourself like a man; Would you really annul My justice?

units.leftText: Or do you have an arm like God? “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity.
units.rightText: Do you have an arm like God’s? Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor,

units.leftText: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him.
units.rightText: Unleash the fury of your wrath; Look on every proud man and humble him;

units.rightText: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. See the strength of his loins

units.leftText: He moves his tail like a cedar. His bones are like tubes of bronze.
units.rightText: His tail sways like a cedar; His bones are tubes of bronze;

units.leftText: He is the chief of the ways of God. Surely the mountains produce food for him,

units.leftText: He lies under the lotus trees, The lotuses cover him with their shade.
units.rightText: He lies under the lotus plants, The lotus plants conceal him in their shade;

units.rightText: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; Can anyone capture him as he looks on,

units.leftText: Will he make many petitions to you, Will he make a covenant with you,

units.rightText: They are joined to one another; His snorting flashes with light,

units.leftText: His breath kindles coals. There is strength in his neck.
units.rightText: His breath sets coals ablaze, Strength resides in his neck,

units.leftText: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. His heart is as firm as a stone,
units.rightText: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; His chest is as hard as a rock,

units.leftText: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail;
units.rightText: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; The sword that reaches him has no effect,

units.leftText: He counts iron as straw, The arrow can’t make him flee.

units.leftText: Clubs are counted as stubble. His undersides are like sharp potsherds,

units.leftText: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes a path shine after him.
units.rightText: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; He leaves a glistening wake behind him;

units.leftText: On earth there is not his equal, He sees everything that is high.

units.rightText: You asked, ‘Who is this You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak.

units.leftText: It was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has. Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”
units.rightText: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has. So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”

units.leftText: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD commanded them, and the LORD accepted Job. The LORD restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends. The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
units.rightText: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer. After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.

units.leftText: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that the LORD had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold. So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
units.rightText: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring. So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

units.leftText: He had also seven sons and three daughters. He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
units.rightText: And he also had seven sons and three daughters. He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.

units.leftText: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers. After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
units.rightText: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers. After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
